metadata.title: Durham Smythe catches only target in Week 1
metadata.description: Durham Smythe caught his only target for four yards in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
metadata.analysis: Smythe saw minimal usage in the Week 1 win, joining rookie Matthew Hibner in finishing behind veteran Mark Andrews in tight end targets in the win. The tight end remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

metadata.title: Durham Smythe - Blocking in Baltimore
metadata.description: The Ravens and Smythe have agreed to terms on a contract, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Smythe had a substantial role for the 2025 Bears as a blocking tight end for both the offense and special-teams unit. He'll now bring that skill set to Baltimore, likely as a replacement for Charlie Kolar, whom the Ravens lost to the Chargers in free agency. The 30-year-old Smythe caught just four passes in 17 games during the 2025 regular season, a number that may increase now that he is paired up with Lamar Jackson in a new Ravens offense.

metadata.title: Durham Smythe signs with Ravens
metadata.description: The Ravens agreed to terms with TE Durham Smythe.
metadata.analysis: Smythe will hold a blocking role in the Ravens tight end room. It is a positive sign for the potential role of Mark Andrews based on the current state of the Ravens tight end room.

metadata.title: Ravens Agree to Terms With Durham Smythe
metadata.description: The Baltimore Ravens agreed to terms on an undisclosed deal with free-agent tight end Durham Smythe on Wednesday, sources told Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. Smythe will likely be the blocking replacement at the position for Charlie Kolar, who left in free agency this week to join the Los Angeles Chargers. The 30-year-old veteran will reunite with new Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle after being coached by him with the Chicago Bears in 2025. The former fourth-round pick by the Miami Dolphins in 2018 out of Notre Dame won't be anywhere near the fantasy radar in any format going into next season. Smythe had a career-low four catches on six targets for 25 yards in 17 regular-season games with the Bears last year, and he has a measly 136 receptions for 1,253 yards and three touchdowns in his eight-year NFL career.

metadata.title: Durham Smythe - Not targeted in finale
metadata.description: Smythe was not targeted in the Bears' 19-16 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Smythe finished the season playing all 17 games and caught four passes for 25 yards on six targets. He has totaled 13 receptions over the last two seasons while serving primarily as a blocking tight end, limiting his fantasy relevance to deep leagues. He is set to hit free agency.

metadata.title: Durham Smythe catches one pass in Week 17
metadata.description: Durham Smythe caught his only target for 11 yards in the Bears' 42-38 loss to the 49ers in Week 17.
metadata.analysis: Smythe has seen minimal involvement in the Chicago passing attack, recording one target or less in each of his last six games. The tight end can remain off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 18 contest against the Detroit Lions.

metadata.title: Durham Smythe - Minimal involvement continues
metadata.description: Smythe caught his lone target for 11 yards in the Bears' 42-38 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Smythe has now recorded one reception for 11 or fewer yards in four of his last seven contests, drawing just one target in this game. Those four catches account for all of his receiving production this season. His role remains too limited to provide reliable fantasy value outside of emergency depth situations.

metadata.title: Durham Smythe catches one pass in Week 14
metadata.description: Durham Smythe caught his only target in the Bears' 28-21 loss to the Packers in Week 14.
metadata.analysis: Smythe remains a non-factor in the Chicago offense, posting one target or less in 12 of 13 contests. The tight end can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 15 contest against the Cleveland Browns.

metadata.title: Durham Smythe - Blocking role holds steady
metadata.description: Smythe caught one pass for two yards on one target in the Bears' 28-21 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Smythe has three receptions this season, all coming over his last four contests and totaling 14 yards. His primary usage as a blocker and third tight-end role keep him as a non-factor in fantasy lineups.

metadata.title: Durham Smythe - Second catch of season
metadata.description: Smythe caught one pass for four yards on one target in the Bears' 31-28 win over the Steelers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Smythe has been used primarily as a blocker this season and his firsts reception came in the last two games despite regular snap involvement. His low route volume and limited targets keep him off the fantasy radar outside of the deepest leagues.
